svg.title: Embedded, cradle-to-gate and embodied carbon compared
svg.desc: Three nested boxes. The innermost, CBAM embedded emissions, covers direct emissions from the defined production processes and the emissions in precursors such as the aluminium in foil, with electricity counted only for cement and fertiliser under the EU CBAM and not at all under the UK CBAM before 2029. The middle box, cradle to gate, adds upstream mining and refining, transport of raw materials, bought-in electricity, packaging and overheads. The outer box, embodied carbon, adds transport to the customer, installation, maintenance and repair, demolition, waste and disposal, but excludes the energy and water used to run the building or product.
svg.text: Embedded, cradle-to-gate and embodied: three boundaries, one product
Each box counts everything inside it. The CBAM box is the narrowest and the only one with a price on it.
Embodied carbon (whole life, except running it)
Adds transport to site, installation, maintenance, replacement, demolition and disposal
Cradle to gate (A1–A3): a product carbon footprint
All emissions to the factory gate, including bought-in electricity and transport of materials
in foil, the clinker in cement)
